newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund volatility supported below 5.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund volatility supported below 5.0 pct.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options traded on LIFFE was slightly higher on Monday after sharp moves in futures on Friday left volatility well-bid, traders said.
Traders said the usual pattern of falling volatility after major economic data had not been followed on this occasion.
"Usually we see a retracement on volatility," said a London-based options broker. "But the massive liquidation we saw on Friday ruled that out."
He said U.S. Treasuries were driven down after central banks took profits and hedge funds sold in the middle of the yield curve, and that weakness fed into European markets.
Debt futures markets initially spiked higher after employment data showed non-farm payrolls rose by 210,000 in October, against a revised drop of 35,000 the previous month.
Brokers said attempts to bid down volatility had come to nothing, with buyers emerging when any slight slide was detected.
"Once volatility comes down below 5.00 percent, people get interested, and lie in wait for it to get down to 4.8 percent where it's a good buy," said the options broker.
"The market reaction to the figures on Friday didn't encourage anyone to offer volatility," he said.
Implied volatility of at-the-money call options was at 4.88 percent at 1500 GMT, compared with 4.86 percent on Friday. January rose to 5.09 percent from 5.03 percent.
A trader at a U.S bank in London said call options ac ross the strikes were well-bid, as investors sought to hedge their forward rate agreements.
According to LIFFE data, more than 2,800 lots were traded at the 99.50 strike and about 350 at the 99.00 strike. Some 2,700 calls were traded at the 100.00 strike, and a further 3,100 at 100.50.
December Bund futures were down nine basis points at 99.45.
"Volatility moves today are a reflection of Friday's rejection of par (100.00)," said the U.S. bank trader. "We see the move higher continuing."
